items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: He -- I didn't know Buster in Memphis, to be frank with you. And along came Buster with W. C. Handy and the St. Louis Blues...

ctx.x: We drove all the way from Memphis to Chicago, Jimmie Lunsford Lunsford, myself and a few other fellows of the Lunsford Lunsford group to catch Louis Armstrong. He was a ball of fire. He had great personality, big, beautiful smile and playing that trumpet. I'm telling you. He was on the order of King Oliver. That was his idol, King Oliver, and he naturally was an idol of so many other modern day trumpet players and guys that came along. From my beginning I always wanted to hear Louis Armstrong, and that man…

And another fellow I was very, very much engrossed in, which I figured was the fastest clarinetist in the world, that was a homey -- hometowner by the name of Buster Bailey. You see, his father disallowed him to play with any other band other than W. C. Handy's. He was the original St. Louis Blues player. He was sitting in the band. He was working with Handy because his father didn't -- didn't want him to go out of town and didn't want him to quit school, going to [Cotchard] High School in Memphis.

He -- I didn't know Buster in Memphis, to be frank with you. And along came Buster with W. C. Handy and the St. Louis Blues, and he was one of the first ones to play St. Louis Blues, and that man to me was the greatest clarinetist in the world. That included all of them. Benny Goodman was -- which Benny can really play. That rascal can play, with the help of John Hammond, of course. And --
